# Insika

> Insika is a Ruby runtime for LLM agents in production: a durable, resumable turn
> pipeline behind an OpenAI-Responses-compatible HTTP API (`POST /v1/responses`), with
> tools, skills, cross-session memory, per-agent policy, content-safety guardrails, and a
> web control UI. Agents are data — created and edited at runtime, no redeploy.

Insika is the operational layer around a model call, not another way to call a model. It
builds on [RubyLLM](https://rubyllm.com) for the chat/tool primitives and adds the parts
production needs: checkpointing, policy, safety, limits, observability and a drop-in API.
Engine overhead is ~0.4 ms p50 per turn.

Every link below is raw markdown — the same files the human-facing site renders at
<https://guizaols.github.io/insika/>. A running instance serves them too, at
`GET /docs/<name>.md` (index at `GET /docs`), alongside its model catalog at
`GET /models.json` and an imperative build-my-first-agent prompt at `GET /start.md`.

## Start here

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/README.md): what Insika is, the one-file first agent, and the router to everything else.
- [Why Insika](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/WHY.md): why a runtime rather than a DIY loop, an assembled framework, or a hosted gateway.
- [Running locally](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/RUNNING-LOCAL.md): boot the engine, the control UI, pointing a Responses client at it, wiring tools to your own backend.
- [Onboarding prompt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/onboarding/start.md): the skill-structured prompt a coding agent follows to build a first agent (served live at `/start.md`).

## Core concepts

- [Agents](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/AGENTS.md): the AgentProfile, its five access layers, and creating or editing agents at runtime via UI, pack import, or `POST /v1/agents`.
- [Tools](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/TOOLS.md): code tools, data-defined tools, MCP import, manifests, and egress troubleshooting.
- [Skills](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/SKILLS.md): the SKILL.md format and progressive, on-demand loading.
- [Context](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/CONTEXT.md): what fills a turn's prompt, the token budget and eviction, cross-session memory.
- [Workflows](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/WORKFLOWS.md): deterministic orchestration of several agents — the five agentic-workflow patterns (sequential, routing, parallel fan-out/fan-in, evaluator-optimizer, orchestrator-workers), schema-validated I/O, durable runs, and when to let the model choose instead.
- [Channels](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/CHANNELS.md): how people reach the agent — the two shapes (native, where the engine speaks the platform, and relay, where you keep your own WhatsApp/Slack stack and the engine only runs the turn), the web widget you install with one `<script>` tag and the mandatory rate limit behind it, the relay's two-route contract, `event_id` dedup, and the at-most-once delivery guarantee.
- [Plugins](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/PLUGINS.md): the two extension tiers — config-only (data tools, MCP, skills) and code (a gem with a manifest that registers tools, policies, middleware or context providers).
- [Architecture](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md): the turn pipeline, the tool-loop, checkpoint recovery, the fiber concurrency model, composition roots.

## Operate in production

- [Security](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/SECURITY.md): the security features — content-safety guardrails, egress guard, approvals, edge limits, secret handling.
- [Sandbox](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/SANDBOX.md): the confined-execution primitive for untrusted tool code.
- [Deploy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/DEPLOY.md): containerized deploy under Falcon, durable SQLite volume, tokens and environment.
- [Observability](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/OBSERVABILITY.md): the event stream, plus opt-in OpenTelemetry — turns as traces and metrics, attribute conventions, dashboard recipes.
- [Evals](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/EVALS.md): the quality harness — a case as YAML data (deterministic assertions plus a rubric a judge scores), cases in the store or the corpus, a panel of distinct judge models with aggregate/min_agreement, and the baseline gate.
- [Refinement](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/REFINEMENT.md): reading an agent's own production traffic back as a ranked failure report — the findings, the window, the privacy rules, and why there is no scheduler.

## Proof

- [Benchmark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/BENCHMARK.md): the neutral, provider-free engine benchmark — methodology, numbers, and how to rerun it without an API key.
- [Load test](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/LOADTEST.md): load-testing the engine end-to-end and comparing data topologies.

## Optional

- [AGENTS.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/AGENTS.md): conventions for an agent working *on* this codebase — commands, layout, binding rules, gotchas.
- [Contributing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): setup, the house rules, and what makes a useful PR.
- [Vulnerability disclosure](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/SECURITY.md): how to report a vulnerability privately, and what is in or out of scope.
- [Changelog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/CHANGELOG.md): pre-release; nothing is tagged yet.
- [Code of conduct](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md): Contributor Covenant 2.1 and the enforcement contact.
